prompt: For application data sent using TCP over IPv4 over Ethernet, which sequence describes encapsulation towards transmission?

options.text: Application data -> Ethernet frame -> IPv4 packet -> TCP segment -> bits
options.explanation: Ethernet is the outer framing in this example. The TCP segment and IPv4 packet are formed before the Ethernet frame.

options.text: Bits -> Ethernet frame -> IPv4 packet -> TCP segment -> application data
options.explanation: This describes the receiving direction towards application data. The question asks about the sending direction.

options.text: Application data -> IPv4 packet -> TCP segment -> Ethernet frame -> bits
options.explanation: TCP and IPv4 are reversed. In this example, IPv4 carries the TCP segment inside its packet.

options.text: Application data -> TCP segment -> IPv4 packet -> Ethernet frame -> bits
options.explanation: Correct. TCP encapsulates the application data, IPv4 carries the TCP segment, and Ethernet carries the IPv4 packet before physical transmission.

source: CAB222 Week 1, Lecture 1 Introduction to Networks_v1.pdf, pages 35, 40, 43, 46 and 49.

prompt: Which addressing fields are included in the Ethernet header at the Data Link layer?

options.explanation: Correct. The Ethernet header includes source and destination MAC addresses for communication on the link.
In this example, IP addresses are in the enclosed IPv4 header, not the Ethernet header.

options.text: Source and destination TCP port numbers
options.explanation: TCP port numbers are in the TCP header. They are not Ethernet addressing fields.
The frame check sequence is error-checking information in the Ethernet trailer. It does not identify the source or destination.

source: CAB222 Week 1, Lecture 1 Introduction to Networks_v1.pdf, pages 14 and 46.
